podcast.title: Life-Altering Accident
podcast.body: In 2005, at the age of 25, Eric Hauk sustained a severe injury when a retaining wall in a friend's Seattle backyard collapsed, causing him to fall 12 feet onto a concrete slab. This accident resulted in three broken vertebrae and paralysis from the sternum down, leaving him permanently unable to walk. "He fell 12 feet and slammed up against a slab of concrete, breaking three vertebrain his back, and paralyzing him from the sternum down."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Return to Stage After Accident
podcast.body: Despite his paraplegia, Eric Hauk was determined to continue playing guitar. Within four months of his accident, he was back on stage performing with his then-band, The Lashes, at a festival. "Within four months of the accident, he was back on stage with his band The Lashes, playing a festival."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Touring Challenges and Outreach
podcast.body: Touring with Portugal. The Man presents significant logistical challenges for Eric, as wheelchair-accessible tour buses and dressing rooms are uncommon in many venues. Despite these obstacles, he and the band persist, and Eric actively engages in outreach to the disabled community while on the road. "Wheelchair accessible tour buses aren't exactly common, nor are addressing rooms for a lot of venues, but Eric and the band haven't let that stop them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
